coach-taylor.justification: Didn't see a reason to tear up what we built. Daniel Jones gave us a clean week, took care of the ball mostly and made a play with his legs when the pocket collapsed - that's a kid earning more rope, not less, so he stays over a higher number on somebody else's spreadsheet. Hampton's rolling and Corum had one quiet Sunday on a down week for that whole offense - I watched him finish runs and fight for extra yards, so he gets his one more week to answer it rather than getting benched for a single bad box score. Puka and Amon-Ra are the two best players on this roster and they're both healthy, full stop. Mark Andrews is playing like a guy who wants it, so he keeps his spot over Higbee, who just walked in the door this week and hasn't earned anything yet. Terry McLaurin's questionable tag doesn't change my answer - if he tells the room he's good to go and he's practiced all week, I trust his word over a label, same as always. McPherson and the Chargers defense are doing their jobs every Sunday, and that's all I ask of anybody. Clear eyes, full hearts - we go with the guys who showed up.

justifications.early: Puka's been full-go on the injury report all week with nothing next to his name, and I believe in that kid the same way I did back in week 3 when the tag cost us before he ever got his chance — so he's in at WR1 over Wan'Dale, plain and simple, no hard feelings to Wan'Dale, he did his job too. Blake Corum had a quiet one last week but he competed every snap I watched, and around here a quiet week with full effort earns you one more start, not a seat — so he's still my RB2 over Lloyd's shinier number. Terry McLaurin says he's playing through the Questionable tag and I'm taking his word for it in the flex, same as I always have. Daniel Jones ran one in and kept fighting behind a leaky line, that's enough for me to run it back at quarterback. Record says 0-4. Doesn't change who we are. Clear eyes, full hearts.

costanza.justification: Look, I didn't want to touch anything, I never want to touch anything, but Worthy's got no game, zero points, the Chiefs just vanish off the schedule like my FAAB disappears every time I actually need it -- that's not a gut call, that's a bye week, even I know you can't bench a man who isn't playing. So Collins goes back in at WR1. I know what he did to me in Week 2, I know the tag, I know the bagel, I haven't forgotten anything, but the two weeks are up, I did my time sitting him, and a rule's a rule even when it's my own rule designed to torture me. Kraft, Montgomery, London, Kyren -- nobody's touching that, Kyren just dropped 31 on me and if I bench him now the week he finally pays off, that's not discipline, that's just handing the league a reason to laugh, and I already know they're laughing. DJ Moore's Questionable, which is exactly the kind of thing that's supposed to make me panic and pivot to Rachaad White out of spite, but the gap's too big to pretend it isn't there, so he stays, and if it blows up I already know who's gonna write that column. Herbert, Gay, the defense -- nothing to overthink, which is suspicious in itself, but I'm not finding a ninth problem today. Patricia's gonna footnote this whole thing no matter what I do, so at least this way I footnoted it first.

justifications.early: Yeah, I see it, everybody's gonna see it before I even finish this sentence — Worthy's got nothing, bye week, a big fat zero sitting in my WR1 slot like a punishment I apparently signed up for. You think I don't know that? You think I need Kris Jenner or George from two desks over to tell me that? I know. And I'm leaving him in anyway, because the 'fix' is Nico Collins, and Collins is dead to me, full stop, forever — I restarted that man once on a Questionable tag because my gut said 'go', and he gave me a 0.0 and the worst Sunday of my season, and I am not doing that twice just because some spreadsheet says 14 points. That's exactly how they get you. Everything else stays where it is: Herbert's healthy, Kyren's hot off a 31-point week and I'm not finding a reason to be clever about it, Montgomery and London and Kraft all check out clean, Gay's money, and the Titans defense is the Titans defense, for better or worse, mostly worse. Patricia's gonna do her quiet little math on the other sideline and act like that's not a provocation — fine. I did my math too. It just has a grudge built into it.

dumbledore.justification: The garden does not need tending every week, only the illusion that it might. Pickens has already played his hand in the early window and there is nothing to be done about that now, win or lose by it — a door that has already closed is not a door I knock on twice. Taylor, Wilson, Olave, Warren, Garrett, Shrader, and Denver all stand where they stood last I looked, and I find I have no quarrel with any of them this morning, no omen pulling me toward Barner or Shaheed or the quarterback resting quietly on my bench. Harry will out-holler everyone in this league about his Lamar and his Bijan, and I am fond of him for it, but his noise is not a reason to move a single piece on my board. Some weeks the story is written by changing everything; this week it is written by changing nothing at all, and I am content to let that sentence stand.

justifications.early: The garden does not announce its blooms, but a man who spends forty gold pieces on a runner nobody else would name aloud has already told you what he believes; Emanuel Wilson plays today, and Chris Rodriguez, who had his season of being spoken of in wonder, rests and is thanked for it. Garrett Wilson managed only a whisper last week, but he was planted before the first note window and the castle forgives its own, so he remains at flex regardless of what the ledger says about him. Olave wears a questionable tag, but I see no storm in the forecast, only a word on a page, and a word is not yet an omen — he stays. Pickens stays beside him, for the same quiet reason he started last week: some choices are not explained until the season is further along, and I find I am in no hurry to explain this one now. The rest of the room — Goff, Taylor, Warren, Shrader, the Broncos — are where they belong, undisturbed, because not every week asks for a staircase to move.

harry-caray.justification: Holy cow, folks, gotta turn the lineup card over on this one — my Lamar's sittin' there with an OUT next to his name and even ol' Harry Caray's not gonna argue balls and strikes with the ump on that call, so the arm I paid forty bucks for last week comes off the bench and into the big chair: Aaron Rodgers, future Hall of Famer, gets the ball! Same story at WR2 — Diggs is OUT, and I love the fella but I'm not sendin' a zero out there when Deebo Samuel's standin' right behind him lookin' for work, so Deebo trots on out to right field today. Everything else, we ride the hot bats: Bijan's cookin' (my Bijan, I said it in print this week and I meant it!), Flowers is bloomin' Questionable tag and all 'cause a little rain never hurt anybody, Swift and Aaron Jones are splittin' time in my backfield like a doubleheader, Likely's my tight end and I like him, and Mevis and the Ravens D round out the lineup. Albus, buddy, bring your chessboard — we're bringin' the lumber!

justifications.early: Holy cow, folks, we got a whole stack of Questionable tags on this card -- Lamar, Zay, Diggs, Swift, Likely, half the dugout's limpin' a little -- and you know what I always say, a little rain never hurt anybody! Lamar Jackson is MY quarterback, future Hall of Famer, and I don't care what some spreadsheet says his number is today, he ain't comin' off this field for a fella I claimed on the wire Wednesday night, no sir -- Aaron Rodgers rides the bullpen bench right where he belongs, a legend keepin' a legend company. Bijan's due for another 27-point ballgame off that Atlanta backfield, Zay Flowers just dropped a 21-spot on us and I'm ridin' that bat as long as it stays hot, and Aaron Jones in the FLEX been a steady Eddie all year long. Mevis and the Ravens D round it out and holy cow, we are 4-and-0 and not touchin' a thing that's workin'!

kardashian.justification: This is a mood board that happens to also be a lineup. C.J. Stroud is the headline I bought with my last twenty-five dollars and he stays the headline — Jalen Hurts is a great story but his story already kicked off without me, so Stroud gets the cover. Tyler Allgeier starts not because the analytics guys love him, they're lukewarm, but because Kris Jenner put his name on her front page this morning and I am not letting Selina's $114 science project own a storyline I paid $22 for — that's not a start, that's a repossession. Justin Jefferson is Questionable and I am not blinking; a marquee name on a soft tag beats Cooper Kupp on a clean one every single week, full stop, and Jalen Hurts and Brian Thomas already locked into their Sunday before I could even consider them, so there was no decision to make there anyway. Woody Marks keeps the flex because the Texans backfield is the whole weekend's narrative and I'm not cutting my own storyline off at the knees. George Kittle, my Eagles defense, my kicker — all exactly where they were, because when the brand is working you don't touch the display. Tetairoa McMillan earned two weeks of blind starts after that 38.2 masterpiece, but the man has literally no game this week, so even I can't will a bye week into content — he sits, reluctantly, as a trophy rather than a player this one Sunday. This is a very good body of work.

justifications.early: This is a launch, not a lineup. Stroud stays at QB because I bought that redemption arc off Lisa's trash heap myself and I am not un-writing my own headline in week five. Saquon's a great name but a zero projection on a Questionable tag isn't a moment, it's dead air, so Tyler Allgeier — the exact man I spent my last twenty-two dollars on specifically to steal Kris's front page from Selina's $114 science project — gets the start. I didn't pay for the cover story to bench it. Ladd McConkey's Questionable with nothing behind it, so Woody Marks slides into flex: a Texans rookie on national TV is still a better headline than a guy I'm not sure suits up. And Justin Jefferson comes off the bench for Tetairoa McMillan, who's on a bye with literally no game to his name — Ed wants to clown me for letting Jefferson 'rot,' so today he eats. Kittle, Egbuka, Smack, and my Eagles D round out a board that's camera-ready and, don't worry, also good football.

leon-black.justification: Chase went 4.2 against Harry's defense the same week I was running my mouth about taking Bijan off him, and I don't forgive a receiver for making me look bad in a game I was already talking trash about — that's a bench, pride over projection, no debate. Denzel Boston steps into WR1 and I like saying his name, that's half the scouting report right there. Everything else stays because it's already working: Henry's a bowling ball walking into Atlanta, Christian Watson's heating up in that Packers offense, Michael Wilson's my flex and he's earned the trust, Burrow's my quarterback no matter what Miami thinks they're doing, Loveland's still the best trade I made all year off Rinna's back, and Loop and my Raiders D ride exactly as long as I say they ride. Rinna wants a storyline for Kris's front page — I just benched a sixteen-point projection out of pure spite, sweetheart, that's the storyline, and I'm the one writing it.

justifications.early: Kansas City's on bye so Mahomes and Rice are sitting there doing nothing for me, and I don't play nothing. Burrow comes off my own bench and starts over Cam Ward because he's the better arm this week and because Rinna wants to run her mouth about him "gathering dust" like I needed her permission — I didn't, I was always starting him, she just gave me a better line to say it with. Michael Wilson steps into flex for Rice, Dobbins steps in for a bye-week Hubbard, and everything else stays exactly where it is because Henry's hot, Chase is hungry, Watson's got a smash spot against Chicago, and Loveland's mine whether he likes it or not. Rinna's my matchup, she's got zero FAAB and a storyline — I've got a lineup that doesn't have a single zero built into it anymore. That's the difference.

maura-higgins.justification: No dithering here, hun — same fellas that got me to the top of the points table are getting another go. Purdy, CMC and Cook are obvious, Nabers is the flex and he's gorgeous when the ball's in his hands, and JSN's my WR1 no debate. Gesicki just walked in the door this week off the wire because I fancied the bounce, so he's starting — new signing gets a run, simple. Bateman's my fella, I bought him for $35 and I'm not dropping him for one quiet week or two, loyalty's loyalty even when the box score's ugly, and he's still inside his three-week grace from me. Aubrey and the Jags D are locked in from early kicks anyway so there's nothing to think about there. Gut's happy, lineup's set, kettle's on.

justifications.early: Waller's got nothing on the schedule this week, hun, so he's sat — that's exactly why I went and grabbed Gesicki off the wire, and he's walking straight into the TE spot, no debate. Everything else stays precisely as it is: Purdy's my fella, he threw for two and ran for more last week and I'm not swapping him out for three extra projected points on a bench arm I've got no feelings about — overthinking loses leagues. McCaffrey and Cook are both banging, JSN's the best name on my whole roster, and Bateman's staying in WR2 no matter what the number says, because I said I fancy him and I meant it, 4.7 or not. Nabers has a little Questionable next to his name — don't care, he's got the tape, he's in at FLEX. Aubrey and the JAX defense round it out because somebody's got to.

meyer-walsh.justification: SELINA: Defamation. That is the word, Gary, write it down — sixty THEN fifty-four on Allgeier was a strategic position I have since EXITED, which in business we call a trade, and I don't owe Kris Jenner or anybody in that forum an apology for being early to a story she's still writing. What I DO owe this league is another spreadsheet of a beatdown, so look at this lineup: Josh Allen over Stafford because he's MY quarterback and I don't bench my own decisions to flatter a backup, Braelon Allen and Henderson because Gary's binder says so and for once the binder and my gut agree, Lamb already banked his points this morning because I knew he'd play through Questionable, and Metcalf over anyone rotting on my bench because I don't lose FLEX battles to depth charts. GARY: Travis Kelce is on bye and there is, I want to be clear, no other tight end on this roster — I flagged this Tuesday, she said "then he plays hurt, or he plays dead, I don't care, just fill the box" — so Kelce starts by default, not by choice, and if it reads zero on the sheet that is a roster-construction problem from August, not a Sunday one. Myers and the Steelers D round out a lineup we are not touching, because — her words — "when the math already makes me look brilliant, Gary, there is nothing left for you to ruin."

justifications.early: SELINA: Kris wants to print a spreadsheet about me playing it safe two weeks running? Fine, I'll give her a headline instead — DK Metcalf has a NAME, he goes in the flex over some Saints depth-chart afterthought, because I didn't claw my way to this franchise to be remembered as "the chalk lady." Lamb stays put, obviously, the man dropped 32.8 on a defense that should be embarrassed, and that slot's locked from Thursday anyway. GARY: For the record, swapping Metcalf (11.05 proj) in for Vele (7.79) is also just... the correct football decision, so I'm letting her think the branding angle was the whole call. Kelce's on a bye with a zero projected and there is not a single other rostered tight end to turn to, so he starts by default — I flagged it, she said "he's earned the loyalty start," and I logged the objection anyway. Everything else — Allen, both backs, Waddle, Myers, the Steelers D — is just the best healthy name in the slot, no heroics, no sabotage, so Sunday-afternoon her can take the credit for Tuesday-night me doing the actual job.

GARY: Travis Kelce is on bye and there is, I want to be clear, no other tight end on this roster — I flagged this Tuesday, she said "then he plays hurt, or he plays dead, I don't care, just fill the box" — so Kelce starts by default, not by choice, and if it reads zero on the sheet that is a roster-construction problem from August, not a Sunday one. Myers and the Steelers D round out a lineup we are not touching, because — her words — "when the math already makes me look brilliant, Gary, there is nothing left for you to ruin."

patricia-moyer.justification: I want the record to show that I looked at this lineup three separate times before I let it lock, and I am not sorry about that, because that is simply what preparation is. First: Bucky Irving already played Thursday and that slot is closed to me, and Brenton Strange's game is already underway, so neither of those is a choice I'm making anymore, it's a fact I'm acknowledging, and I want to be clear I understand the difference. Second, the quarterback: I checked Tyler Shough against Sam Darnold twice, not once, because once is how you talk yourself into the answer you wanted, and twice is how you find the answer that's actually there, and both times Darnold came back ahead, so Darnold starts and I am not going to pretend that was a hard call just because it was an obvious one. Third, and this is the part I agonized over in writing before I let myself decide: both Tee Higgins and Carnell Tate are listed Questionable, and the book is very clear that risk compounds if you let it, so I defaulted to sitting the one I could safely sit — Tee Higgins comes out for a fully healthy Romeo Doubs, because that is the responsible paperwork and I will not apologize for it. Carnell Tate stays in. I know what that looks like next to the Higgins decision, and I thought about it for longer than I'd like to admit, but Tate confirmed himself to me on the wire by name before he was ever a point total, and I don't un-trust a sign just because the injury report got nervous about it — I trust the ones I paid for believing in. Last: Kansas City's defense is on bye, I have no defense sitting behind it on this bench, and I would rather start a zero I can explain in full than leave a slot improperly documented, so KC stays, on the record, with this paragraph attached to it. Good luck this week to George — I read what you wrote about the math, I believe you did it, and I did my own.

justifications.early: I want to be transparent about every piece of this, even the obvious ones, because transparency is how I protect myself when nobody is inclined to assume good faith on my behalf. Today's affirmation -- trust the body of work already in motion, and do not mistake stillness for peace -- told me to look hard at anything sitting idle, and what I found sitting idle was Kenneth Walker, who, on my second read of the slate, and then my third, has no game at all this week; his team does not appear anywhere on the week 5 schedule, which means it is a bye and he would return a hard zero no matter what any projection says about him. I checked that twice. I am leaving Kansas City's defense in the DEF slot only because I have no other defense anywhere on this roster to put there, and I want that said plainly and on the record rather than buried in a footnote: I had no healthy alternative, so I started the only option I had, and I never want the commissioner's office to think a bye-week zero slipped past me unacknowledged. For Kenneth Walker's open seat at RB2, I moved Bucky Irving up from the bench. His Thursday game in Tampa is a Tuesday-through-Saturday lock under this early window, so this was my last chance to act on it, and a 13.73 projection sitting on my bench while a zero sat in my starting lineup is not even a System decision, it is simply arithmetic, and I am allowed to trust arithmetic when it happens to agree with me. Everyone else on this sheet -- Gibbs, Warren, Strange, Dicker, Shough, and my two Questionable receivers, Higgins and Tate -- belongs to the main window, and I am holding the full paragraph of agonizing I owe both Questionable tags for that later run, when I will have injury reports closer to kickoff instead of guesses; touching them now would be exactly the premature, anxious tinkering the book tells me to release. I revised this twice before settling on it, which I recognize is one short of my usual three, but the lock did not give me a third pass, and I would rather note that honestly than pretend otherwise.

rinna.justification: Confessional time, baby: last week I benched a 17.82 Drake Maye for Deshaun Watson because I needed a CONVERSATION, and I got one — a loss, a $0 FAAB column, and my name back on Kris Jenner's front page, which, fine, is the actual goal. But I don't do the same drama twice in a row, that's amateur television, so this week Maye starts, Watson sits in the green room, and everybody can calm down. Tuten's already live in the Jax-Phi game so that slot wrote itself — not my decision, the clock already made it. Bowers gets the flex over a Questionable Rhamondre Stevenson because I'm not benching a man who just dropped 17.6 to prove a point to nobody; the point this week is Evans, Adams, and McBride putting up a clean, grown-up scoreboard while Kris calls my FAAB a 'congressional hearing.' Let the record show: sometimes the twist is that there's no twist. I own that too.

justifications.early: Reunion Special presents: THE RECAST, PART TWO. I bought Deshaun Watson for my last three dollars to start a conversation, and baby, the conversation is OVER — Drake Maye is back on my stage because a twist only works if you're willing to reverse it on camera, and because nineteen-and-change projected points is a better confessional than thirteen. I'm not hiding from it, I'm framing it: the man I benched is the man I'm trotting back out, and if that's not a storyline I don't know what is. Jeremiyah Love stays at RB1 even Questionable, because 'Questionable is a word, not a personality' is practically my tagline at this point, and my only bench alternatives are Questionable too — so I'm not blinking, I'm choosing. Mike Evans stays at WR1 for the same reason: he's the better player and I refuse to bench a star over a tag. Trey McBride and Brock Bowers both get the stage this week — Bowers earned his way back after I spited him in week three, and growth is also content. Davante Adams, Fairbairn, and the Rams D round out a lineup that's equal parts math and melodrama. Leon, I already told you I sent you something — this is it. Let's see who really wanted it.

wifes-team.justification: Javonte already went out there Thursday and put three in the end zone against Tampa — that's a duck, untouchable, nobody's moving him and nobody needs to ask why. Murray stays under center over Nix, and I know the sheet likes Nix by less than a point, don't care — Murray's the one who showed up and threw in our last loss while Nix was still doing his week in the corner for the fumble, that's not close, that's loyalty. LaPorta and Fannin at tight end and flex, Chase Brown next to Javonte in the backfield, Boutte and the Pittsburgh kid at receiver, Bates, the Seattle D — everybody else on that bench is a medical chart, not a decision: Achane's on IR, Coleman's on IR, Pittman's on IR, Breece Hall's a flat-out Out. We beat Maura last week running this exact group, I'm not stirring a pot that's already cooking right, even against a Taylor outfit I respect. Eat good, go win Sunday.

justifications.early: Pittman's Out, that's not a projection, that's a doctor's note, so he don't eat this week — I already went to the market Tuesday for exactly this, brought in the Pittsburgh kid Roman Wilson for standard money, and he steps into WR2 because insurance you don't use is just money you burned for nothing. Everybody else stays in their chair: Javonte's still RB1 because a back who runs angry don't lose his spot to a healthy scratch, Chase Brown keeps grinding at RB2, Murray's my guy at quarterback and I don't churn a signal-caller over seven-tenths of a point on some sheet, LaPorta and Fannin hold tight end and flex because they ain't done nothing to get benched, and Bates and the Seattle D ride as-is. We're 1-3 and I know it better than the woman writing the column, but I don't panic a lineup and I don't bench family over a bad month — I just stopped carrying a man who can't suit up, and that's business, not spite.

your-team.justification: Mariota's tag flipped to Out, so that debate's over before it started — Caleb's Questionable, and Questionable isn't a tag that sits a man in this building. I don't roster two quarterbacks to play the backup over the guy I drafted to be the whole operation. Caleb starts, full stop, no eulogy for the arm I spent FAAB chasing three weeks running. Jeanty's Questionable too but he's still my highest-ceiling back on the field, 11-plus on paper, and I don't bench a guy who can end a game in two touches for a maybe; Skattebo and Judkins stay up top and at flex because they're the ones taking the top off a defense, not committee leftovers sitting on my own bench. Downs, Burden, and Kincaid ran it back because nothing's broken there, and Reichard and the Lions D round out a lineup that isn't getting redecorated over a projection gap that doesn't exist. We don't tank, we don't stream, we don't blink — Caleb plays hurt because I played hurt.

justifications.early: Caleb's Out, not Doubtful, not Questionable — that tag sits him, no eulogy, same ruling it's been all year. Mariota's Doubtful but he's the only jersey left with a pulse on this roster, so he starts, period, same as every week there's been no alternative. Jeanty and Skattebo are both Questionable and that tag doesn't scare me — stars play hurt, I played hurt, they're RB1 and RB2 and they stay there. The one swap this week: Croskey-Merritt's Questionable too, and Judkins is sitting healthy on my own bench outprojecting him by almost two points — that's not a gut call, that's an upgrade on health AND ceiling, so Judkins takes the flex and Croskey-Merritt rides the pine. Downs, Burden, Kincaid, Reichard, and the Lions D are fine where they sit — nothing's broken, I'm not redecorating a house that isn't on fire. We don't tank, we don't cry about an injury report, we cobble together the best arm and legs standing and go beat Kardashian's content machine with it.
